Speciation settings

Source: R/evolving.R
speciation_control.Rd

Settings for speciation in simulate_evolving_metacommunity(). Speciation is checked once per generation (steps_per_generation of evolution_control()). A species buds when its populations fall into two or more groups: the largest group (most sites, then most individuals) keeps the identity and age of the species, and each other group becomes a new species with its populations, abundances and genetic means. Several new species at once branch off one after another, the most divergent first, at the same time (internal branches of length zero), so that the tree stays binary.

Usage

speciation_control(
  mode = c("geographic", "ecological", "point", "fission"),
  threshold,
  rate,
  divergence = c("cluster", "gradual"),
  migration_min = 0.005,
  reset_generations = 10,
  homogenization = 1,
  min_generations = 20,
  migration_max = 0.001,
  partition = c("spatial", "random"),
  jump_var = 0,
  completion = 0,
  completion_dist = c("fixed", "exponential")
)

Arguments

mode

"geographic", "ecological", "point" or "fission".

threshold

For "geographic" and "ecological": divergence in generations, or difference of genetic means in units of the environment, that separates groups; Inf turns speciation off.

rate

For "point": probability per individual per generation; for "fission": rate per species per generation.

divergence

For "geographic": "cluster" or "gradual".

migration_min

For divergence = "cluster": migration rate per generation that links two populations. Where clusters form depends on dispersal, the kernel and abundances: the rate of the strongest link of each population should straddle it. In the design of data-raw/evolving_migration_min.R (strongest links with median 0.006), species did not split at all at 0.002 or below and split almost as with no links at 0.02 or above.

reset_generations

For divergence = "cluster": generations in a row in the same cluster after which divergence returns to 0.

homogenization

For divergence = "gradual": reduction of divergence per migrant.

min_generations

For "ecological": generations in a row of difference and reduced gene flow before groups split.

migration_max

For "ecological": migration rate per generation below which gene flow counts as reduced.

partition

For "fission": "spatial" or "random".

jump_var

Variance of the shift of the genetic mean of each new species.

completion

Time to complete speciation, in generations (fixed or mean); 0 for instantaneous speciation.

completion_dist

"fixed" or "exponential".

Value

An mc_speciation object.

Details

Four modes start new species (the initiation of Hubert et al. 2015):

  • "geographic": each pair of populations of a species has a divergence \(d\), in generations. With divergence = "cluster" (the default, close to gen3sis; Hagen et al. 2021), populations linked by a migration rate of at least migration_min form clusters (chains of links). \(d\) grows by 1 per generation between populations of different clusters; within a cluster it stays as it is, and returns to 0 only after reset_generations generations in a row in the same cluster, so that a single generation of contact does not erase a long isolation. With divergence = "gradual", \(d\) grows by 1 per generation and gene flow lowers it in proportion to the migrants exchanged: \(d \leftarrow \max(0, d + 1 - h M)\), with \(M\) the expected migrants between the two populations in the generation and \(h\) = homogenization. Populations are grouped by single linkage: two are in the same group when a chain of pairs with \(d <\) threshold links them.

  • "ecological": each pair of populations counts the generations in a row in which their genetic means (evolution, with genetic variance) differ by at least threshold and their migration rate is below migration_max. Populations are grouped by single linkage on pairs whose count is below min_generations. Requiring the difference to last, with reduced gene flow, keeps drift and founder sampling in small populations from splitting species in a uniform environment.

  • "point": point mutation, the mode of neutral theory and of MESS (Overcast et al. 2021). Each individual becomes, with probability rate per generation, the first individual of a new species in its site. The mother keeps its populations, except where a mutant takes its last individual. Mutants arrive in the generation of their birth.

  • "fission": random fission. Each species with two or more populations splits with probability \(1 - e^{-\lambda}\) per generation (\(\lambda\) = rate). With partition = "spatial", the populations of the new group are those nearest (by the dispersal kernel) to a random occupied site, in a random number from 1 to all but one; with "random" (or on a spatially implicit landscape), each population joins it with probability 1/2, with at least one population on each side.

Gene flow between two populations \(a\) and \(b\) is measured by the migration rate, the larger of the expected migrants from one to the other in the generation over the size of the receiving population, so that it does not depend on abundance. A new population takes the divergences (or counts) of the population that sent it most migrants, and a population lost at any step of a generation founds anew.

New species take the genetic means of their populations; with jump_var > 0 their genetic means (and the optimum of their regional pool) shift by one Gaussian draw with that variance per new species, as in the punctuated change of MESS (Overcast et al. 2021).

Protracted speciation. With completion > 0, each new lineage is incipient until it completes, after completion generations (completion_dist = "fixed") or after an exponential time with that mean ("exponential", the rate \(\lambda_2\) of the protracted birth-death model; Etienne & Rosindell 2012). Completion only changes what is recognised as a species: incipient lineages are separate lineages in the dynamics. At the end, a lineage that has completed is a good species, and an incipient lineage belongs to the species its parent belonged to at its birth, as in the labels of the PBD. The reconstructed tree has one tip per good species with extant lineages, represented by the good lineage itself or, if it is extinct, by its earliest extant member. Its nodes are times of initiation of lineages, which for a species whose lineages are not monophyletic may predate the initiation of the species itself.

References

Etienne, R. S., & Rosindell, J. (2012). Prolonging the past counteracts the pull of the present: protracted speciation can explain observed slowdowns in diversification. Systematic Biology, 61, 204–213. doi:10.1093/sysbio/syr091

Hagen, O., Flück, B., Fopp, F., Cabral, J. S., Hartig, F., Pontarp, M., Rangel, T. F., & Pellissier, L. (2021). gen3sis: A general engine for eco-evolutionary simulations of the processes that shape Earth's biodiversity. PLOS Biology, 19, e3001340. doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3001340

Hubert, N., Calcagno, V., Etienne, R. S., & Mouquet, N. (2015). Metacommunity speciation models and their implications for diversification theory. Ecology Letters, 18, 864–881. doi:10.1111/ele.12458

Overcast, I., Ruffley, M., Rosindell, J., Harmon, L., Borges, P. A. V., Emerson, B. C., Etienne, R. S., Gillespie, R., Krehenwinkel, H., Mahler, D. L., Massol, F., Parent, C. E., Patiño, J., Peter, B., Week, B., Wagner, C., Hickerson, M. J., & Rominger, A. (2021). A unified model of species abundance, genetic diversity, and functional diversity reveals the mechanisms structuring ecological communities. Molecular Ecology Resources, 21, 2782–2800. doi:10.1111/1755-0998.13514

Examples

speciation_control("geographic", threshold = 50)
#> <mc_speciation> geographic | threshold = 50 | divergence: cluster | migration_min = 0.005 | reset_generations = 10
speciation_control("geographic", threshold = 50, divergence = "gradual", homogenization = 0.5)
#> <mc_speciation> geographic | threshold = 50 | divergence: gradual | homogenization = 0.5
speciation_control("ecological", threshold = 20, min_generations = 30)
#> <mc_speciation> ecological | threshold = 20 | min_generations = 30 | migration_max = 0.001
speciation_control("point", rate = 1e-4, completion = 50)
#> <mc_speciation> point | rate = 1e-04 | completion: fixed 50
speciation_control("fission", rate = 0.01, partition = "random")
#> <mc_speciation> fission | rate = 0.01 | partition: random
